title: LLM escape-hatch: micro-reversion & emergency rollout checklist (working)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for emergency escape-hatches (micro-reversions) during LLM feature rollouts, canaries, and A/B tests. Focus is on fast, safe, minimally-invasive actions product + SRE + oncall can take to stop customer-visible regressions while preserving data integrity and enabling a quick path to recovery.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated inference paths surfaced through the Console rollout machinery and Redwood API.
- Not a replacement for full incident runbooks — this is the *traffic escape hatch* layer for model/feature regressions.
- Assumes standard telemetry (per-route latency/error, token-level cost, sample-level eval hooks) present and baseline established.

When to consider activating the escape hatch (examples):
- Latency P95 > 2x SLO for > 3 minutes on a canary cohort
- Error-rate (500/502/timeout) spike > 10x baseline on cohort slice
- Large-scale quality regression detected by golden-prompts (drop in pass-rate > 15%)
- Safety/policy hits (content-moderation flags) > threshold or novel pattern emerges
- Cost runaway (token burn > budgeted threshold) for new model variant

Primary escape-hatch mechanisms (ranked by destructiveness & reversibility):
1) Traffic throttle and progressive drain (preferred first step):
   - Reduce cohort allocation to 0.5x or pause new activations for the flagged slice.
   - Command: console rollout set-slice --id <slice> --rate 0.1
   - Goal: slow the blast radius while preserving traceability.
2) Canary reversion to pinned stable model (micro-reversion):
   - Swap model version for the slice to last-known-good (LKG) variant.
   - Command: console rollout apply --slice <slice> --model <LKG-model-id> --defer 30s
3) Route fallback to lightweight fallback model (safety or policy-fallback):
   - Route degraded traffic to a smaller, heavily-moderated model or filtered pipeline.
4) Feature flag toggle (response-level mitigations):
   - Turn off newly-introduced prompt-enrichment, reranker, or system promps via per-route flags.
5) Read-only / queued mode:
   - Convert route to queueing mode to accept but not immediately serve (useful for very high cost/latency spikes).
6) Hard cut (circuit-breaker):
   - As last resort, remove the feature route from the public surface and return stable generic response.

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference):
- Release Owner (PO / Product): assess user-impact, approve reversion, coordinate comms. Owner: usually listed in rollout metadata.
- Oncall SRE: execute traffic controls, confirm infra health, coordinate with infra/serving runtime.
- ML Engineer / Model Owner: validate model issue, prepare LKG model and follow-up patch.
- Customer Success / Account Lead: notify impacted customers if SLA-affecting.
- Observability lead: run targeted telemetry sweeps and generate triage artifacts.
- Incident Communicator: draft and publish status updates (Slack #incidents + Ops page).

Runbook: Detection -> Verify -> Activate -> Communicate -> Remediate -> Postmortem
1) Detection (automated or human):
   - Alert fires (console-signal:latency-slo-violation OR golden-eval-failure)
   - Pager to oncall with immediate context: route id, slice id, recent commits, model id
2) Quick verify (3–5 min):
   - Triage: Are errors systemic or cohort-specific? Check per-country, per-platform, per-tenant splits.
   - Reproduce with 3 golden queries from the canary set against current and LKG model.
   - Collect logs: last 1k requests for slice, sample model outputs, policy flags.
3) Decide: throttle vs revert vs fallback
   - If latency + infra resource pressure -> throttle first.
   - If quality or safety regression confirmed -> revert or fallback immediately.
4) Activate escape hatch (play-by-play):
   - Oncall SRE executes traffic throttle (console command) and monitors errors/latency for 5 minutes.
   - If no improvement, issue micro-reversion to LKG. Document model ids and times.
   - Short-circuit any downstream rerankers or expensive post-processing.
5) Communications (immediate):
   - Slack: @here in #oncall with one-line summary + action taken + who is owning next steps. Template below.
   - Update rollout status in Console (status = degraded / rollback in progress).
   - Notify CS for customers > contract-SLA or notable accounts.
6) Triage & remediation:
   - ML owner runs root-cause experiments (compare prompts, decode settings, quantization artifacts).
   - If bug in prompting/feature: prepare targeted hotfix; validate against golden set in staging.
   - If model quality: consider retraining/reprompting and controlled canary.
7) Postmortem & roll-forward plan:
   - Within 72 hours: blameless postmortem, timeline, decision rationale, follow-up tickets (owner assigned).

Quick comms templates (copyable):
- Slack incident starter: "INCIDENT: observed high-quality regression on rollout <rollout-id> affecting slice <slice>. Action: throttled traffic 2026-02-28T14:03Z, micro-reversion to <LKG-model> at 14:08Z. Owning: @AvaChen, @EthanB. Triage in progress — see <link-to-runbook-or-jira>."
- Customer note (CS): short plain text noting degraded experience and mitigation; include ETA for follow-up.

Observation & instrumentation checklist (before / during / after):
- Golden prompt harness: run top 100 golden prompts across both current and LKG; compute pass/fail delta.
- Token-level cost dashboard: watch for >20% deviation from expected per-session budget.
- Safety flags: list of top 10 new moderation rules triggered.
- Latency histograms (P50/P95/P99) broken down by model, seq-len, tenant.
- Sample logging enabled for 1% of traffic to preserve privacy budget but provide human-inspectable traces.

Synthetic traffic & rehearsal plan (drills):
- Quarterly tabletop + annual live drill with simulated progressive degradation.
- Drill script: introduce slow kernel on dedicated pool -> validate throttle -> revert -> postmortem.
- Measure drill metrics: time-to-detect, time-to-throttle, time-to-revert, customer-facing-impact (simulated).

Testing preconditions (what to validate in staging before enabling auto-escape):
- LKG model artifacts available and pre-warmed in same region as canary.
- Rollout metadata includes stable model id field and pre-deploy check.
- Alerts have high-fidelity filters to avoid noisy flaps (dedupe, lookback).

Common pitfalls & mitigation notes (lessons learned):
- Flap loop: rapid toggling between models -> add cooldown (minimum 10m between full reverts).
- Silent data loss: cut-to-queue mode must gracefully accept and redeliver requests. Test under load.
- Partial rollback surprises: reranker mismatch after revert (ensure backward compat layer for rerank gradients).
- Permission friction: oncall cannot execute reversion because ACL not set — ensure 1-2 runway operators per rotation.

Operational knobs & example commands (placeholders):
- console rollout throttle --slice <slice> --pct 10 --reason "latency-spike"
- console rollout revert --slice <slice> --to-model <LKG-model-id> --force --note "emergency micro-reversion"
- console route set-flag --route <route> --flag disable-reranker
- infra api drain-pool --pool <pool-id> --grace 60s

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Decide default cooldown windows (10m? 30m?) and whether product team can request overrides.
- Should we support automatic golden-prompt-triggered reversion? (pros: faster; cons: false positives).
- Establish per-tenant rollback SLAs and CS notification thresholds.
- Add an automated smoke-run after revert that runs a small set of production-like prompts to validate.

References & background notes:
- See linked JIRA RED-2345 for the incident that inspired this playbook.
- Console rollout API docs: confluence:console-rollouts-api (placeholder).

Quick notes to self (informal):
- We should add a "safety-fallback" tag on models that are approved for immediate fallback. Make an approvals flow.
- Consider a lightweight web UI in the Console showing one-click escape-hatch actions (throttle / revert / fallback) with auto-populated reasons.
- Ask SRE to simulate a model-quality regression next sprint as part of chaos-testing.

Owner: Ava Chen (product) — reach out to @ava on Slack for clarifications.
